mainNote.text:
How to read this canvas

• Every artboard links ONE shared stylesheet, project/happymix.css. It is the deliverable: tokens + components, ready to replace wwwroot/css/dashboard.css.
• Class names (hm-*) map 1:1 to Razor partials listed on the Foundations board.
• Numbered pins (1, 2, 3…) on desktop mockups match the sticky notes beside each row.
• Today mockups are clickable: change the times or hit a preset to see the overnight preview update.
• JavaScript budget: ~40 lines total (range preview, presets, unsaved-changes flag). Everything else is plain forms, links, <details> and CSS :has().

noteServers.text:
Server picker

1  Last-used server sorts first. The card title is a link to Availability, so the most common task is a single tap.
2  Today status line (from the user's saved windows) answers "did I already set it?" without opening the server. Mint dot = set, hollow ring = not set.
3  Settings renders only when CanConfigure (Discord Administrator). Secondary button + Admin badge.
4  Header: brand icon is the home link; Sign out stays a POST form.

Mobile: cards stack, both actions stay ≥44px tall, Sign out becomes an icon button with aria-label.

noteSettings.text:
Server settings

1  Three groups: Server defaults, Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2. Desktop: sticky section nav. Mobile: sticky chip row.
2  Inherited values: dashed control border + "Inherited" badge + the effective value spelled out ("Server default · #announcements"). Overridden values get a solid border, "Custom" badge and a Reset link.
3  The magic strings default / none become a 3-way radio (Inherit · Custom · None). CSS :has() reveals the text field only for Custom; the controller maps back to the same strings.
4  Validation sits under the field it belongs to (aria-invalid + aria-describedby). A short summary at the top links to each error.
5  Channel pickers list only standard Discord text channels HappyMix can post in, prefixed with #.
6  Sticky save bar: "Unsaved changes" flag (tiny JS), Discard (link reload) and Save settings — always within reach.

noteStates.text:
States

Empty → explain why and give exactly one next step.
Error → say what failed and where; keep the user's input; never clear the form.
Saved → role="status" banner, mint, names what was saved ("You're available Today 17:00 → Tomorrow 00:30"). Auto-focus it after redirect so screen readers hear it.

Banners are tinted panels with an icon and a title — the colour is never the only signal.

noteToday.text:
Today

1  Today and Weekly are two views behind a segmented control — real links (?view=today / ?view=weekly) with aria-current="page", no JS.
2  Native <input type=time>, 52px tall, tabular numerals. Mobile gets the OS wheel/clock picker for free.
3  Active time zone sits right beside the inputs. "Change" is a <details> with the existing IANA datalist; empty = server default.
4  Live preview: ~15 lines of JS. End ≤ start ⇒ "Tomorrow" + Overnight badge + duration. Equal times show an inline error and disable Save.
5  Presets only fill the inputs; nothing saves until the user presses Save today.
6  One-off windows list with Remove (POST action=remove).

Mobile: Save today is pinned to the bottom, always in thumb reach.

noteWeekly.text:
Weekly timetable

1  One row per day, Monday first. Times are big tabular numerals; a 24-hour bar beside them makes the week scannable at a glance.
2  Overnight windows run to the end of the bar with a square edge; the next day shows the spill-over as a hatched segment (pattern, not just colour).
3  Edit opens the row in place: server-rendered via ?view=weekly&edit=Wednesday#wednesday. No modal, no JS.
4  Clear is a per-day POST form (action=clear) with aria-label "Clear Wednesday hours".
5  Empty days say "No hours" and offer + Add hours in the same spot Edit would be.

Mobile: each day is a card; Edit/Clear are 44×44 icon buttons with labels for screen readers.
